validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Both findings were re-measured on HEAD at 7ee139f rather than taken on the reviewer's word. The line widths, the ambiguous pronoun and the absent release note are all confirmed by reading the files. The comment replacement is prescribed as literal final lines with measured character counts, so the implementer has nothing to decide. The only judgement in the plan — add a Maintenance release note rather than record an exemption — is argued from the repo's own precedent and the reviewer, not from taste, and the route already keeps a review stage precisely so it can be disagreed with. validated_work_order.understanding: Issue #66 carries two review findings left open by the review of PR #65, and I re-checked both on HEAD (7ee139f) before planning. (1) The beforeEach comment block in packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts is badly rewrapped: measured widths for lines 23-31 are 78, 79, 79, 71, 78, 50, 79, 78, 6, so line 28 is a 50-character stub in a block otherwise wrapped at 71-79, and line 31 is a 6-character orphan. The clause spanning 26-28 reads 'but before the / beforeEach below re-armed it, from the second test on, global.fetch was the / real jsdom fetch again', where 'it' has no antecedent inside its own clause - the nearest singular noun is 'the global.fetch spy' two clauses back at line 24, so a reader can plausibly attach it to init() or to sql.js. That sentence is the one this comment exists to justify, so it is the one that has to be unambiguous. (2) The repo has a release-notes convention (packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105, 'Add a release note', with no documented test-only exemption) and a validating gate at packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs that refuses a diff adding no note under upcoming-release-notes/; PR #65 added none. I decided to satisfy the convention rather than exempt the change, on the evidence that this fork's own sibling follow-up PR #60 shipped upcoming-release-notes/fix-command-bar-dialog-console-drain.md for a purely e2e-test change. Nothing here is user-visible, nothing runs in the browser, and no product behaviour changes.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The work order that produced PR #65 prescribed the replacement comment as pre-wrapped literal text; inserting it changed the paragraph's line breaks without reflowing, so 're-armed it' landed as 're-armed it, from the second test on, global.fetch was the' / 'real jsdom fetch again. patchFetchForSqlJS is a'. The pronoun was in the prescribed wording too, so this is a suggestion on the order as much as on the code - this plan reflows the paragraph and names the referent. The missing release note is the same shape: the convention at packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105 has no test-only exemption, and PR #65 shipped a test-only diff without one.
validated_work_order.approach:
Two files, both decided in full. Nothing is left for the implementer to word.

1. Reflow lines 27-28 of the beforeEach comment in packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts. Replace exactly those two lines; lines 23-26 and 29-31 stay byte-identical. The paragraph as a whole becomes the nine lines below, at the measured widths shown:

  78  // The afterEach below calls vi.restoreAllMocks(), which is file-scoped rather
  79  // than spy-scoped, so it takes down the global.fetch spy this file's beforeAll
  79  // installed along with the console spies. Nothing breaks today, because init()
  71  // has already run and sql.js caches the compiled wasm — but before the
  73  // beforeEach below re-armed the fetch patch, so from the second test on,
  71  // global.fetch was the real jsdom fetch again. patchFetchForSqlJS is a
  79  // vi.spyOn(...).mockImplementation(...) with no restore of its own, so calling
  78  // it once per test is idempotent and the blanket restore can no longer outrun
   6  // it.

Two wording changes, both in service of the two complaints: 're-armed it' becomes 're-armed the fetch patch', so the referent is named rather than left for the reader to infer; and one 'so' is added after the comma, which lifts line 27 from 70 to 73 columns. Without it, dropping 'the' to line 27 would put line 26 at 67 and line 27 at 70, both under the block's 71 floor; 'so' makes the causal chain explicit and keeps every line except the untouched final '// it.' inside 71-79. Do not touch line 31's 6-character orphan - the reviewer asked for the paragraph to end as it does today, and it is a sentence-ending line, not a mid-paragraph stub.

2. Add upcoming-release-notes/clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md, exactly:

   ---
   category: Maintenance
   authors: [Shivam-Fl]
   ---

   Rewrap the sql.js test setup comment so it names the fetch patch instead of a pronoun

   'Maintenance' is the category the review itself named, and it is in categoryOrder in packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs un-autocorrected; the body is a single line and phrased as a command, both required by validateFile in packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs. The author is Shivam-Fl because every other note this pipeline has written in this repo credits the owner, and because findNonPersonAuthors refuses 'claude' and 'github-actions' - the commit and PR bot logins are not valid authors here.

Scope note on the release note: it covers THIS diff, which is the diff the gate checks. PR #65 is merged and its own missing note cannot be retro-satisfied, because a note added today would publish #65's change in whichever release it lands in. What this PR establishes is the going-forward precedent for test-only follow-ups in this series: they carry a Maintenance note.

No product code, no test code and no UI is touched, so there are no interface states to name, no contract to shape, and no new test cases - the existing 16-case web sqlite suite is the regression guard and the change is comment-only.

The one thing a reader cannot check mechanically: that the reworded sentence is still factually true of the code. Read it against the beforeAll/beforeEach/afterEach above it in the same file and say so explicitly in the report - a comment that has drifted from the code is the failure mode this whole ticket exists to prevent.

The reworded sentence must stay factually true of the code. If someone later reads 'the fetch patch' as naming something other than what patchFetchForSqlJS installs, the comment gets worse than the pronoun did - so the QA pass should confirm the referent is the global.fetch spy installed in beforeAll.

The note must not credit the bot. packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs refuses 'claude', 'github-actions' and any login ending in '[bot]' as an author, and upstream Actual publishes authors verbatim as @<author>, so a bot there ships as thanks to a tool.

Adding a Maintenance note for a comment rewrap is a judgement, not a defect fix. It will appear in a published changelog under Maintenance, which is more visible than the change itself. The alternative - record an exemption instead - is one line in out_of_scope below, and the review stage exists to overrule this call.
No host is added: this change makes the app send no data anywhere, and no new request appears, so env.api_allowlist in .sdlc/config.yml needs no edit and QA will not be blocked on it.
out_of_scope: A release note for PR #65 itself. That PR is merged; a note added now would publish its change in a later release than it shipped in, and no fix can reach the diff the gate already passed. The note added here covers this diff.

Line 26's 71 columns. That is the block's existing floor, not a defect introduced here; moving text across it is what pushes line 26 to 67 and line 27 to 70.

alternatives_considered.approach: Settle the release-note finding by recording an exemption on the issue instead of shipping a note, on the grounds that this change is pure comment whitespace with no user-visible effect and the sibling PR #55 shipped without one.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: PR #55 is a single precedent against three that did ship notes (#53, #60, #59), and #60's note is entirely about e2e-test changes - so the practice in this fork is that test-only changes carry a note, not that they are exempt. packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md lists 'Add a release note' among the four things to do when opening a PR with no test-only exemption written anywhere under packages/docs/docs/contributing/, and the gate that enforces it refuses a diff with no note at all. Exempting the category by assertion would leave the convention exactly as unenforced as it is now. Recorded here rather than acted on because the review stage is where that call belongs.

alternatives_considered.approach: Rewrap the whole paragraph from line 23, including lines 29-31, so the '// it.' orphan also goes away.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer explicitly asked for the last two lines to stay untouched so the paragraph ends as it does today. Reflowing them would widen the diff past the finding and change a sentence the reviewer singled out as correct.

alternatives_considered.approach: Name the referent as 'the global.fetch spy' rather than 'the fetch patch', since that phrase already appears at line 24 and is the nearest antecedent.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: 're-armed the global.fetch spy' reads as though the beforeEach re-armed the spy rather than the replacement patch, which is a different (and wrong) claim - patchFetchForSqlJS installs a new spy over global.fetch; it does not re-arm the existing one. 'the fetch patch' is the name the surrounding code and comment already use (see the 'Last on purpose' comment at line 448, which says 'the beforeAll's patch').

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop 'the beforeEach below' to 'the beforeEach' while reflowing, tightening the clause.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It removes a locator a reader relies on - the comment sits above the beforeEach and refers to it as 'below' throughout - and it does not help the wrap: line 27 would fall to 67 columns, further under the floor.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a unit test asserting the comment block's line widths, so the finding cannot regress.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A test that measures the width of a comment is a test of the formatter, not of behaviour; it would fail every time anyone reflows the prose for any reason and teach the next reader to avoid editing the comment. The reviewer's concern was readability, which a width assertion cannot express. Naming the referent is likewise not machine-checkable - it is a QA read, which is why AC-1's how_to_verify asks for the widths to be measured and the sentence to be read.
